notes.title: The Lost One Chronicles - Update Info
notes.notes: [p]Hi everyone,[/p][p]I’m excited to share some details about our upcoming content update: [b]The Lost One Chronicles[/b]. This update focuses on the journey of Lost One dinosaurs as they carve their path toward Dominion. [/p][p][/p][p][b]The Lost One Chronicles[/b] is a [b]free update[/b] that aims to give the Lost Ones a greater sense of meaning, transforming them from hidden dinosaurs into former rulers on a path to reclaim their dominion. Their task is to fully reclaim their region, and completing it will reward you with a special Dominion skin. These skins are exclusive to Lost One dinosaurs and serve as a mark of mastery and completion that further sets them apart.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43691934/184bdbfcff1c183cc2917eeaa18f7453aa9a399d.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Alongside this, we’re introducing a new [b]Challenge mechanic[/b] where enemies deal more damage, but you’ll earn extra XP for the added difficulty.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43691934/1613983779d2ade694aad09277a53197e5acb4c4.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We’re also rolling out another round of [b]dinosaur rebalancing[/b]. The goal here is to make the difficulty curve between tiers feel more gradual and rewarding, so progression feels smoother and more rewarding.[/p][p][/p][p]This is a moderately sized content update and we plan to release this by the [b]End of this year[/b]. [/p][p][/p][p]Dinosaurs Dominion has really helped me grow as a developer, and I want to thank you all for the support. Currently I’m working on this while balancing other projects as well, so the next post you'll see will most likely be update itself. And for longtime fans of Arcupion Art, especially if you’ve played our older games, one of these might just be interesting.[/p][p][/p][p]And that's currently it for this Devlog and more updates coming soon![/p][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: New Update - LIVE! Home Button and AI Rebalancing
notes.notes: [p]Hi everyone,[/p][p]It’s been a month since the release of Dinosaurs Dominion, and during that time I’ve received a lot of valuable feedback from you all, which has helped me spot bugs and issues that slipped through at launch. This update focuses on addressing some of those areas while adding a few quality of life improvements to make your experience even better.[/p][p][/p][p]With that said, here’s what’s new in this update:[/p][list][*][p][b]Home Button[/b]. You can now [b]teleport back to your starting location without losing progress[/b]. This is especially helpful if you ever get stuck during exploration. [i](Note: The Home Button will not be available while in hostile territories.)[/i][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43691934/6fc1034af8e4c6c6a8dd089d208a53cc2adaede0.gif"][/img][/p][/*][*][p][b]AI Balancing[/b] Adjustments. Smoothed out the difficulty curve between Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 AI Dinosaurs. Previously the jump from Tier 1 to Tier 2 used to feel too steep, while Tier 2 to Tier 3 wasn’t as noticeable. Now, the [b]difficulty curve should be more linear and incremental[/b], with a steady uptick in challenge at each tier.[/p][/*][*][p][b]UI Improvements.[/b] The UI is now anchored more consistently, providing better support for a wider range of resolutions. (Note: Ultra wide support isn’t ready yet.)[/p][/*][*][p]Additional Fixes & Adjustments[/p][list][*][p]Dinosaur slope tolerance refined[/p][/*][*][p]Combat settings adjusted[/p][/*][*][p]Additional small in-game patches[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p]Dinosaurs Dominion has been an amazing experience to work on and I’m truly grateful you’ve stuck with the project, as it gives me the chance to keep creating these budget friendly dinosaur games that, hopefully, offer something unique.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you so much for all your support and more updates coming soon![/p]

notes.title: Full Release Update - LIVE!
notes.notes:
[p][b]Hi everyone![/b][/p][p]The [b]1.0 update is now LIVE![/b], and [b]Dinosaurs Dominion is officially out of Early Access[/b]! [/p][p][/p][p]It’s been quite a journey getting here, and we want to thank everyone who’s supported us along the way. If you purchased the game during Early Access, you’ll receive the full version [b]update for free. [/b][/p][p][/p][p]For returning players this update is essentially a [b]complete overhaul[/b] of the previous version. As mentioned in our earlier devlog, Version 1.0 brings a fresh new experience across the board, from combat and exploration to visuals and polish.[/p][p][/p][p]With that said,[/p][p][/p][h2]What [i][b]Is[/b][/i] Dinosaurs Dominion?[/h2][p]It’s a game born from a simple dream I’ve carried for years:[/p][p]
[b]What if the dinosaur roster of [/b][i]Warpath: Jurassic Park[/i][b] could actually go on an adventure like the ones in [/b][i]The Lost World Jurassic Park The Game[/i][b]?[/b][/p][p][/p][p]I loved both [i]The Lost World[/i] and [i]Warpath[/i], but each left me wanting more. TLW gave atmosphere and exploration, but only a handful of playable dinosaurs. Warpath had a full roster but no freedom, just battles in arenas.[/p][p][/p][p]Dinosaurs Dominion is my answer to that gap.[/p][p][/p][p]It’s a love letter to those games, reimagined as a focused single-player adventure where every dinosaur can fight and explore. However, exploration and combat alone may not be enough, it needed direction. I wanted something that felt [b]primal, but purposeful[/b]. Not just survival for survival’s sake, but a goal that taps into the instinct of an actual animal. That’s where the idea of [b]dominion[/b] came in. [/p][p][/p][p]So in essence, [b]Dinosaurs Dominion[/b] is a [b]solo action-adventure[/b] where you [b]play as a dinosaur[/b] on a journey to [b]reclaim the wilds. [/b][/p][p][/p][p]It is made for players who love [b]compact, single-player experiences[/b]. The kind of game where you jump in, play, and walk away feeling like you [i]did[/i] something meaningful. If you’re into [b]single runs, challenging combat, [/b]and[b] rewarding exploration[/b], Dinosaurs Dominion might be exactly your thing.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h2]The Wilds Await[/h2][p]Once again, thank you for your support. There’s more to come in the future, but For today, we simply want to pause and appreciate this moment. The game is finally complete, and we’re excited to share it with all of you. We hope the world we’ve built brings you as much joy as it brought us to create. so, have fun out there, the wilds await.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]⚠️ Important Note:[/h3][list][*][p]You may need to [b]quit and restart Steam[/b] for the update to appear.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Old save files may not be compatible[/b] with Version 1.0.[/p][/*][*][p][b]If you're upgrading[/b] from a previous version, we [b]strongly recommend starting a new game[/b] for the best experience.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Full Release Update - LIVE!
notes.notes:
Version 1.0 for Dinosaurs Dominion is now LIVE!

Added:
[list]
[*] 14 playable dinosaurs, from nimble scouts to towering juggernauts, each with a playstyle defined by size, power, and mobility.
[*] 13 mutations that let you evolve, specialize, and experiment.
[*] 3 open-world maps, each with unique biomes and environmental storytelling.
[*] Focused one-on-one combat inspired by Souls-like design.
[*] Roguelite progression with single-run challenges and permanent impact across journeys.
[*] Landmarks, relics, and remnants that reward exploration with meaningful discoveries.
[*] Totems and trophies, unlockable rewards that reveal deeper insights into the world.
[/list]

notes.title: Progress Update
notes.notes:
Hi everyone, I wanted to give an update on how things are with development. 

In our last post, we’ve mentioned that we're going to take a step back to see where we should take development further in order to bring value and improve player experience. Based on your feedback and upon tinkering with the game further we’ve decided to focus our efforts on the core gameplay loop and workflow as these are possibly the two most important components in terms of the game being a product and a project. We’ve managed to overcome some challenges and made several improvements to the game and we’re excited to show them to you in this post! So lets get started.


[h2]Combat and Locomotion[/h2]

With Dinosaurs Dominion being a simple and compact game, Combat and Locomotion is by far the most important component for us to get right. Because of this we’ve spent the majority of our time testing, refining, and thinking of ways to further enhance the current combat and locomotion system.  So far we’ve managed to implement several improvements to our combat system which not only fixed several bugs but also introduced new mechanics that betters player - AI interaction. Here’s a video showcasing elements we’ve fixed and improved:

[previewyoutube=_la0uuUhpvQ;full][/previewyoutube]

The first is attack - hitbox reaction. After a few tests and tinkers we’ve managed to create a solution that both fix and improve combat detection for both player and AI characters, allowing for more accurate hit detection.

The next is character slope orientation. This allows both players and AI dinosaurs to rotate / orient based on the angle of the surface they're currently on, which makes for better visuals and feel when traversing steep areas. With the combat system improved, integrating the slope orientation system becomes possible as it allows us to have accurate attacks and reactions even on steep surfaces.

The last is additional combat improvements. This is where we focus our attention in finding ways to further improve the interaction between players and AIs during combat. One of the ways we found to further improve this is by having an evasion system for the AI which allows the AI to escape when the player is too close. The subject of Combat improvements is still very much on going as its tied to many other elements including level design and animation which we haven't delved too much into at the moment and will be our main focus moving forward.


[h2]Lighting and Workflow[/h2]

The goal of Dinosaurs Dominion has always been to create compact experience that’s both enjoyable and immersive for players. One of the key ways we can improve from a visual / immersion standpoint is to improve the lighting and post processing. 

Currently much of the visual fidelity of DD is heavily influenced by its post processing. This has resulted in several challenges especially regarding texture consistency. Before the model is brought into Unity it has to go through several programs, in our case we use ZBrush Core for modeling, Topogun 3 for retopology, Blender for UV unwrap, rigging, and animation, and Substance Painter for texture painting (and occasionally baking). 

In other words, by heavily relying on post processing, the visuals of our models look very different in these programs (Substance Painter) than to how they look in Unity. We are fully aware that some differences are inevitable as these programs may have different systems to how they compute lighting and shaders, however, being able to mitigate this will greatly help streamline development as we’d have more consistency.

Because of this we’ve decided to move away post processing based workflow to lighting based workflow, what this means is that the lights and lighting system in Unity will do much of the heavy lifting for the visuals / theme while post processing will be used only to enhance the visuals. This has allowed us to not only have better consistency between our programs but create a much more natural looking atmosphere.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43691934/d48d47a4a1c599d3efe060c0acd6de30ebf12ed8.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43691934/a32f97f26cc25496dc4f3bef4a86e80825ffa7b9.png[/img]


[h2]Development[/h2]

The update to our lighting system resulted in us having better texture consistency between programs. Having this consistency has enabled us to create models more efficiently (less back and forth). As a result we feel more confident growing the list of creatures for the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43691934/c9aaac7b683b9eaf35bba9faa51c933400c7e7aa.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43691934/3eecabd90d1a4e62899a8c188683c92f3deea402.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43691934/898ea83603cd3e4852bfc09c3090ded3ef4f7070.png[/img]

These models are still heavily work in progress and will be worked on further as development progresses. 

We are still in the early stages of our RnD and there’s still a bunch more we need to cover. We’re excited as to where this will take us and we look forward to letting you all know when we’ve made more progress and improvements for the game.

That’s currently it for this devlog and more updates coming soon!

notes.title: The Riverside (Update Info)
notes.notes:
Hi everyone, 

I would like to share a bit of info regarding the next update! so lets get started


[h2]Features in Progress[/h2]

The next update will feature a brand new playable section of the map, the River View and River Side (Entrance). The integration of these segments adds more length and variety to the map. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43691934/2481c8fec4284eb0702f3fc0c737aa43f7950f36.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43691934/cfb7c1fb947185bb849a891ba3c5acf21cecd602.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43691934/ce3d7925a264f43f287884356315d96ba48f2233.png[/img]

In addition, this update will bring a new Player Boost system that, when unlocked, will boost either the player’s stamina or adrenaline, and new AI dinosaurs, the baryonyx and baryonyx alpha. Currently, the baryonyx are still very heavily in the works, however, with the segments done, I can shift my focus towards its integration.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43691934/a3481ef9cbb4bac13ad11cc09080a74a8e58bb40.png[/img]

If everything goes accordingly, this update is aimed to be live sometime in February, so be sure to follow this game to not miss out on any news and info.

That’s currently it for this post and more updates coming soon!
